description: Use this when the user asks for a technical SEO audit, a site crawl or an SEO health check of a website, or for broken links, redirect chains, duplicate or missing titles and meta descriptions, canonical, noindex or hreflang problems, sitemap errors, pages that are hard to find from the home page, or whether robots.txt or meta robots tags keep search engines out of pages. Takes a site address (a domain such as example.com or a full URL; the scheme is optional) and starts a crawl of that site, then returns an audit_id, the page limit and a time estimate to relay to the user. The crawl follows robots.txt, is rate limited, and takes a few minutes for a small site and longer for a large one. The number of pages crawled is capped; the report says when the cap was reached. If the address redirects (http to https, or to www), the final site is audited. Only use it for sites the user owns or is allowed to audit. Do not use it for backlinks, keyword rankings, Google Search Console or analytics data, or writing content: Sitewalk does not measure those. Optional render_scripts (true or false, default false): set it to true only when the user asks for the pages to be read after their scripts have run, as a browser shows them. The server decides whether that is possible for this site and says in the result how the pages were read; report that line as given. Leave it out otherwise. To read a finished audit, use get_audit_report instead.
name: start_site_audit
title: Start site audit
